sections.skill: Write success criteria and use them to revise

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: What are success criteria?

choices.text: A short list of checkable requirements
The number of times you asked
The tool's own rating of its answer

questions.correct_answer: A short list of checkable requirements
questions.intro: A first answer is a DRAFT. To improve it, decide what "good" means before you judge it: write SUCCESS CRITERIA, a short list of checkable requirements such as "mentions all three options," "under 200 words," "no jargon," "includes a deadline." Then compare the draft against each criterion and ask for specific changes ("the deadline is missing; add it to the first paragraph"). Specific feedback works better than "make it better." Criteria also help you compare two drafts fairly, by scoring each against the same list instead of picking the one that simply sounds nicer.

sections.skill: Score a draft against a checklist

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: Which criterion did the invitation miss?
questions.intro: Scoring against a CHECKLIST is simple: read each criterion, look at the draft, and mark it MET or NOT MET. Example criteria for an invitation: (1) gives the date, (2) gives the place, (3) says how to reply, (4) under 80 words. Draft: "Join us Saturday at Lakeside Park! Bring a snack." Date: met (Saturday). Place: met (Lakeside Park). How to reply: not met. Under 80 words: met. Score: 3 of 4. The missing item tells you exactly what to ask for next.

questions.domain: Foundation 4: Asking for what you need
questions.prompt: After you asked for an added deadline, the new draft has the deadline but lost the location. What does this show?

choices.text: The first draft must have been perfect
Recheck all criteria after each revision

questions.correct_answer: Recheck all criteria after each revision
questions.intro: Revising can go wrong in a few ways. Each new draft may fix one problem and quietly break another, so recheck all criteria, not only the one you asked about. Repeated "try again" requests without feedback can produce drafts that are different but not better. And a draft can meet every stated criterion while still being wrong about facts, because criteria about format do not check truth. Include accuracy in your criteria when it matters, and stop revising when the criteria are met.
